```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

This article applies the whole workflow of must, from the design to the
methods paragraph, to two outdoor mesocosm experiments whose data come with
the package: Polazzo & Rico (2021), with an insecticide, a herbicide and
nutrient enrichment, and Hermann et al. (2024), with an insecticide and
three temperature regimes. `vignette("must")` explains each step; here the
emphasis is on the choices that each data set asks for and on how to read
the results. The analyses illustrate the package and do not replace those of
the original articles.

Each analysis follows the same steps:

1. `describe_design()`: what the design identifies, with the samplings taken
   before the stressors were applied declared in `baseline`.
2. `fit_responses()`: one model per response, with its error distribution
   chosen for the data.
3. `suggest_null_models()`: the null models that the guidelines of Schäfer &
   Piggott (2018) give for what is known about the stressors and for the
   effects of each stressor alone, estimated from the model.
4. `estimate_interactions()`, `classify_interactions()` and
   `compare_null_models()`: the interactions, their classes and whether the
   null models agree on them.
5. `report_interactions()`: the methods and the table of decisions.

What `suggest_null_models()` needs to know about the stressors is the same
in both experiments. The stressors do not act similarly, and one of them
acts specifically on physiology: chlorpyrifos (an inhibitor of
acetylcholinesterase) and diuron (an inhibitor of photosystem II) in the
first experiment, imidacloprid (which binds to the nicotinic acetylcholine
receptors of insects) in the second. The responses are densities, counts and
a loss of mass, not mortality, and with a single concentration of each
pesticide the stressor-effect relationships are not known. How the
sensitivities to the stressors are distributed and correlated is not known
either: those criteria are left unknown, so that every value is tried.

```{r setup}
library(must)
suggest <- function(fit) {
  suggest_null_models(fit, similar_action = FALSE, specific_action = TRUE,
                      mortality = FALSE, stressor_effect = FALSE)
}
```

The residual checks of `fit_responses()` are switched off
(`residual_checks = FALSE`) only so that this article runs without the
DHARMa package; in an analysis, keep the default.

## Insecticide, herbicide and nutrients

Polazzo & Rico (2021) used 24 outdoor mesocosms, three per combination of a
full factorial of chlorpyrifos (1 µg/L, or absent), diuron (18 µg/L, or
absent) and nutrients (nitrogen and phosphorus added twice a week, or
ambient). The nutrient additions started four weeks before the pesticides
were applied, on day 0.

```{r polazzo-stressors}
stressors <- c("insecticide", "herbicide", "nutrients")
control <- c(insecticide = "absent", herbicide = "absent", nutrients = "ambient")
```

### Phytoplankton

`polazzo_phytoplankton` has the density of each taxon and their total on
days -5, 7, 15 and 50. Day -5 precedes the pesticides but not the nutrients,
so it is a baseline for the pesticides only. Declared per stressor in
`baseline`, it stays in the model, and no interaction that involves a
pesticide is tested on it.

```{r phyto-design}
phyto_design <- describe_design(polazzo_phytoplankton, stressors, control,
                                unit = "mesocosm", time = "day",
                                baseline = list(insecticide = -5, herbicide = -5))
phyto_design$sets[, c("set_id", "stressors", "net_identifiable", "pure_identifiable")]
```

The full factorial identifies the three pairwise interactions and the
three-way one, whose pure interaction can be separated from the pairwise
ones. The densities are whole numbers, which `fit_responses()` would take
for counts; as densities, counts scaled to a volume (the source does not
give the unit), they are declared continuous in `response_types`.

```{r phyto-fit}
phyto_fit <- fit_responses(polazzo_phytoplankton, "total_density", phyto_design,
                           response_types = c(total_density = "continuous"),
                           residual_checks = FALSE, seed = 1, quiet = TRUE)
phyto_fit
phyto_fit$fits$total_density$reason
```

A Gamma model with a log link fits best. The variance of its random
intercept per mesocosm was estimated at zero, and the intercept was removed.

```{r phyto-suggest}
phyto_choice <- suggest(phyto_fit)
phyto_choice$null_models
table(phyto_choice$sets$type, phyto_choice$sets$time)
```

The guidelines leave the three null models of Madge Pimentel et al. (2025):
simple addition (AD), the multiplicative model (MU) and dominance (DO). The
stress addition model needs mortality as the effect, concentration addition
stressors that act similarly, and dominance stays because the correlation of
the sensitivities is unknown. In most sets and days the single effects are
too uncertain to have a direction (types of Piggott et al. 2015); on day 15
the insecticide alone increased the phytoplankton.

```{r phyto-estimate}
phyto_est <- estimate_interactions(phyto_fit, null_models = phyto_choice, n_sim = 4000,
                                   seed = 2021)
e <- phyto_est$estimates
# Effects of each stressor alone, as multiples of the control density
single <- e[e$order == 3L & e$component == "single" & e$null_model == "MU",
            c("time", "stressor", "estimate", "lower", "upper", "p_adjusted")]
single[c("estimate", "lower", "upper")] <- round(exp(single[c("estimate", "lower", "upper")]), 1)
single$p_adjusted <- signif(single$p_adjusted, 2)
single
summary(phyto_est)
```

```{r phyto-numbers, include = FALSE}
fold <- function(s) single$estimate[single$time == "overall" & single$stressor == s]
```

On single days none of these effects is significant once the p-values are
adjusted across sets and days, but averaged over the samplings the
insecticide alone multiplied the phytoplankton by `r fold("insecticide")` and
the herbicide alone by `r fold("herbicide")`. Few interactions deviate
from the null models, mostly in the averages over time:

```{r phyto-agreement}
phyto_agreement <- compare_null_models(phyto_est)
phyto_agreement[phyto_agreement$agreement %in% c("robust", "model_dependent", "conflicting"),
                c("time", "stressors", "estimand", "AD", "MU", "DO", "agreement")]
phyto_classes <- classify_interactions(phyto_est)
phyto_classes[phyto_classes$time == "overall" & phyto_classes$null_model != "DO",
              c("stressors", "null_model", "single_codes", "code_interaction", "class")]
```

`plot()` with `type = "models"` draws them under each null model, as
deviations relative to the control; here the three pairs averaged over the
samplings (the three stressors together, whose bloom dwarfs them, are left
out):

```{r phyto-models, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5.5}
pairs <- unique(e$set_id[e$order == 2L])
plot(phyto_est, type = "models", time = "overall", set_id = pairs)
```

The mean densities explain them:

```{r phyto-means}
after <- polazzo_phytoplankton[polazzo_phytoplankton$day > 0, ]
treatment <- paste(after$insecticide, after$herbicide, after$nutrients, sep = " / ")
phyto_means <- round(tapply(after$total_density, list(treatment, after$day), mean))
phyto_means
```

```{r phyto-bloom, include = FALSE}
bloom <- round(phyto_means["chlorpyrifos / diuron / added", "7"] /
                 phyto_means["absent / absent / added", "7"])
```

* **Herbicide and nutrients.** Diuron alone increased the phytoplankton,
  nutrients alone did not change it on average, and together they kept it at
  or below the density of the controls. Averaged over the samplings, every
  null model flags this deviation (`robust`), and the classes call it a
  negative synergism (−S) under AD and MU.
* **The two pesticides.** Only dominance flags their interaction
  (`model_dependent`): whether it deviates depends on the mechanism assumed,
  and the guidelines leave that open because the correlation of the
  sensitivities is unknown.
* **The three stressors.** Their net deviation is not significant, but the
  pure three-way interaction is positive under AD and MU: with the three
  stressors together the phytoplankton bloomed (on day 7, `r bloom` times
  the density with nutrients alone) beyond what the pairwise interactions
  explain.

### Macroinvertebrates

`polazzo_macroinvertebrates` counts the individuals of each taxon on days
-32, 15, 30 and 50. Day -32 precedes every stressor, so it is a common
baseline. Besides the total, the analysis follows *Cloeon*, a mayfly, an
insect group sensitive to organophosphate insecticides such as chlorpyrifos.

```{r macro-fit}
macro_design <- describe_design(polazzo_macroinvertebrates, stressors, control,
                                unit = "mesocosm", time = "day", baseline = -32)
macro_fit <- fit_responses(polazzo_macroinvertebrates, c("total_abundance", "cloeon"),
                           macro_design, residual_checks = FALSE, seed = 1, quiet = TRUE)
macro_fit
```

Both are counts, and the negative binomial fits both; the total of one
sample is missing in the source and that sample is left out. The guidelines
leave the same three null models:

```{r macro-estimate}
macro_choice <- suggest(macro_fit)
macro_choice$null_models
macro_est <- estimate_interactions(macro_fit, null_models = macro_choice, n_sim = 4000,
                                   seed = 2021)
summary(macro_est)
```

```{r macro-numbers, include = FALSE}
taxa <- names(attr(polazzo_macroinvertebrates, "taxa"))
share <- round(100 * sum(polazzo_macroinvertebrates$physella_acuta, na.rm = TRUE) /
                 sum(polazzo_macroinvertebrates$total_abundance, na.rm = TRUE))
```

The total, `r share`% of which are the snail *Physella acuta*, shows no
effect and no interaction. *Cloeon* tells another story:

```{r cloeon}
day15 <- polazzo_macroinvertebrates[polazzo_macroinvertebrates$day == 15, ]
with(day15, tapply(cloeon, list(insecticide, paste(herbicide, nutrients, sep = " / ")),
                   paste, collapse = ", "))
e <- macro_est$estimates
e[e$response == "cloeon" & e$order == 3L & e$component == "single" & e$null_model == "AD",
  c("time", "stressor", "estimate", "p_adjusted", "status")]
with(e[e$response == "cloeon" & e$component == "interaction", ], table(status, time))
```

Two weeks after the application, chlorpyrifos had eliminated *Cloeon* from
every mesocosm but one. The effect of the insecticide alone is then tested
from the probability of observing only zeros if *Cloeon* had kept the
density of the controls (`status = "boundary"`; adjusted p < 0.001). The
interactions that need the mesocosms with the insecticide alone cannot be
measured on that day (`not_estimable`): once a stressor alone has eliminated
the response, nothing is left on which the other stressors could add or
multiply. From day 30 the effect of the insecticide is no longer detected,
and no interaction is detected either. A community total can hide the loss
of its most sensitive taxa.

## Insecticide and heat

Hermann et al. (2024) used 24 outdoor mesocosms, four per combination of a
2 x 3 factorial: imidacloprid (nominal 1 µg/L, applied on days 0, 14 and
28, or absent) and temperature (ambient; elevated, 4 °C above ambient; or three
heatwaves of 7 days, separated by 7 days at ambient temperature). The
temperature treatments lasted until day 42, and the following six weeks
were a recovery phase. The water temperature measured in the evening shows
the heatwaves, on days 3, 17 and 31:

```{r hermann-temperature}
evening <- hermann_water_quality[hermann_water_quality$time_of_day == "evening", ]
round(tapply(evening$water_temperature, list(evening$temperature, evening$day), mean), 1)
```

Temperature has three levels, so the design gives two contrast sets:
imidacloprid with elevated temperature and imidacloprid with heatwaves, each
against ambient temperature.

```{r hermann-stressors}
h_stressors <- c("imidacloprid", "temperature")
h_control <- c(imidacloprid = "absent", temperature = "ambient")
```

### Zooplankton

`hermann_zooplankton` has the density of each taxon and their total, sampled
the day before the first application (day -1, a baseline for both
stressors) and every two weeks after it, a few days after each heatwave
during the heat phase.

```{r zoo-design}
zoo_design <- describe_design(hermann_zooplankton, h_stressors, h_control,
                              unit = "mesocosm", time = "day", baseline = -1)
zoo_design$sets[, c("set_id", "stressors", "levels")]
zoo_fit <- fit_responses(hermann_zooplankton, "total_density", zoo_design,
                         residual_checks = FALSE, seed = 1, quiet = TRUE)
zoo_fit
zoo_choice <- suggest(zoo_fit)
zoo_choice$null_models
```

A non-significant interaction is not evidence of additivity. To ask whether
the combination follows a null model, a margin is declared, here generously:
deviations smaller than half the density of the reference combination are
taken as negligible (`margin = 0.5`; see "Additive, or only not detected?"
in `vignette("must")`).

```{r zoo-estimate}
zoo_est <- estimate_interactions(zoo_fit, null_models = zoo_choice, n_sim = 4000,
                                 seed = 2024, margin = 0.5)
e <- zoo_est$estimates
# Effects of warming alone, as multiples of the density at ambient temperature
warming <- e[e$component == "single" & e$stressor %in% "temperature" &
               e$null_model == "MU" & e$time != "overall",
             c("time", "levels", "estimate", "lower", "upper", "p_adjusted")]
warming$levels <- sub(".*temperature=", "", warming$levels)
warming[c("estimate", "lower", "upper")] <- round(exp(warming[c("estimate", "lower", "upper")]), 2)
warming$p_adjusted <- signif(warming$p_adjusted, 2)
warming
```

The heatwaves reduced the zooplankton to about a third of its density at
ambient temperature on the three samplings of the heat phase, and elevated
temperature on the first two; after the heat phase the densities recovered.
The intervals of those effects exclude no change, but their adjusted
p-values are just above 0.05: intervals are not adjusted for the twelve sets
and times, p-values are.

```{r zoo-interactions}
summary(zoo_est)
rel <- e[e$component == "interaction" & e$null_model == "MU" & e$time != "overall",
         c("time", "levels", "relative", "relative_lower", "relative_upper")]
rel$levels <- sub(".*temperature=", "", rel$levels)
rel[3:5] <- lapply(rel[3:5], round, 2)
rel
```

No interaction deviates from any null model after the adjustment, and none
is equivalent either: every verdict is inconclusive. The relative deviations
under MU, (observed − expected) / reference, have intervals far wider than
±0.5. With four mesocosms per combination and densities this variable, the
experiment cannot tell additivity from interactions as large as the effects
of the stressors themselves.

With `type = "time"`, `plot()` follows each set over the samplings: the
effects of each stressor alone and the expected and observed combined
effects (top), and the interaction with its class (bottom), here under MU:

```{r zoo-time, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 6.5}
plot(zoo_est, type = "time", null_model = "MU")
```

### Chironomids

The larvae of the chironomids recorded in `hermann_macroinvertebrates`
(Chironomini, Orthocladiinae and Tanypodinae) are added into one count.
Macroinvertebrates were sampled a week before the first application (day
-7) and every two weeks after it.

```{r chiro}
macro_h <- hermann_macroinvertebrates
macro_h$chironomidae <- macro_h$chironomini + macro_h$orthocladiinae + macro_h$tanypodinae
chiro_design <- describe_design(macro_h, h_stressors, h_control, unit = "mesocosm",
                                time = "day", baseline = -7)
chiro_fit <- fit_responses(macro_h, "chironomidae", chiro_design, residual_checks = FALSE,
                           seed = 1, quiet = TRUE)
chiro_fit
chiro_est <- estimate_interactions(chiro_fit, null_models = suggest(chiro_fit),
                                   n_sim = 4000, seed = 2024)
summary(chiro_est)
before <- macro_h[macro_h$day == -7, ]
round(tapply(before$chironomidae, list(before$imidacloprid, before$temperature), mean), 1)
```

Neither stressor alone has a detectable effect on the larvae, and no
interaction is detected. Before the treatments, the mesocosms assigned to
the control already held about three times as many larvae as most of the
others: with four mesocosms per combination, chance differences among
groups of mesocosms are as large as many treatment effects.

### Leaf litter decomposition

Leaf litter in coarse-mesh bags, open to macroinvertebrates, lost mass by
microbial decomposition and by macroinvertebrate feeding.
`mass_loss_percent` is the share of the initial 2 g that each bag lost; one
bag gained mass, and its percentage is missing in the source.

```{r litter}
litter <- hermann_leaf_litter[hermann_leaf_litter$process == "macroinvertebrate feeding", ]
litter_design <- describe_design(litter, h_stressors, h_control, unit = "mesocosm",
                                 time = "day")
litter_fit <- fit_responses(litter, "mass_loss_percent", litter_design,
                            residual_checks = FALSE, seed = 1, quiet = TRUE)
litter_fit
litter_choice <- suggest(litter_fit)
litter_choice$models[, c("null_model", "status")]
writeLines(strwrap(litter_choice$models$reason[litter_choice$models$null_model == "MU"], 80))
```

Here the guidelines exclude the multiplicative model. The effects of the
stressors alone are far from the effect limit (no decomposition at all),
their sum never exceeds it, and the effect is not mortality: neither step 5
nor step 6 of the guidelines, which lead to MU, is reached. The null models
suggested depend on the effects estimated for each response, not only on
what is known about the stressors.

```{r litter-estimate}
litter_est <- estimate_interactions(litter_fit, null_models = litter_choice, n_sim = 4000,
                                    seed = 2024)
summary(litter_est)
e <- litter_est$estimates
# Effects of warming alone on the mass lost, in percentage points
warming <- e[e$component == "single" & e$null_model == "AD" &
               e$stressor %in% "temperature" & e$time != "overall",
             c("time", "levels", "estimate", "lower", "upper", "p_adjusted")]
warming$levels <- sub(".*temperature=", "", warming$levels)
warming[c("estimate", "lower", "upper")] <- round(warming[c("estimate", "lower", "upper")], 1)
warming$p_adjusted <- signif(warming$p_adjusted, 2)
warming
```

The heatwaves increased the loss of mass by 12 to 18 percentage points on
the collections of days 25, 39 and 81, and no interaction with imidacloprid
is detected.

## Methods and decisions

`report_interactions()` writes the methods of each analysis from its
objects. For the zooplankton of Hermann et al. (2024), with its classes and
the agreement among null models:

```{r report}
zoo_report <- report_interactions(zoo_est, classes = classify_interactions(zoo_est),
                                  agreement = compare_null_models(zoo_est))
cat(zoo_report$methods, sep = "\n\n")
zoo_report$decisions[!zoo_report$decisions$source %in% c("default", "recorded"),
                     c("decision", "value", "source")]
```

## What the two experiments show

* **Few interactions survive.** With three or four mesocosms per
  combination, several contrast sets and several samplings, few
  interactions remain significant once the p-values are adjusted. Averages
  over the samplings (`time = "overall"`) are more powerful, as for the
  herbicide and nutrients on the phytoplankton.
* **Not detected is not additive.** The tests of equivalence on the
  zooplankton of Hermann et al. (2024) were all inconclusive, even with a
  margin of half the reference density.
* **The null model decides some interactions.** The interaction of the two
  pesticides on the phytoplankton deviates only from dominance: only a
  mechanistic hypothesis about the correlation of the sensitivities can say
  whether it is an interaction.
* **The suggestion depends on the data.** Within the same experiment, the
  guidelines left AD, MU and DO for the zooplankton and only AD and DO for
  leaf litter decomposition, because the effects of the stressors alone
  differ between the responses.
* **Totals can hide sensitive taxa.** The total of the macroinvertebrates
  did not change while chlorpyrifos eliminated the mayfly *Cloeon*, whose
  interactions could not be measured on that day.
